title: Ledger Mapper Identity and Conversion Contract
objective: Freeze pure Domain/ORM Mapper boundaries, logical repository identity, deterministic ChangedFile/ChangedSymbol technical IDs, conversion/error/version rules, and all-eleven-family round-trip requirements without implementing Mapper code.
scope: Normative Mapper Contract v1 for all eleven frozen Ledger domain and ORM object families.
Machine-readable standard-library-recomputable ChangedFile and ChangedSymbol identity vectors.
Context validation, Project Memory, immutable Run, targeted regression tests, and one independent local commit.
explicit_non_goals: No to_domain, from_domain, Mapper class, Mapper registry, mappers package, or production conversion function.
No Domain, ORM, Repository, Session, Unit of Work, migration, schema/table, database connection, Parser/Indexer, Git consistency, API, or UI implementation.

No accepted ADR, Manifest schema, dependency, lockfile, runtime configuration, business domain, Factor Lab, TDX, Dataset Snapshot, Factor DSL, Optimization, Validation, Registry, LightGBM, or Qlib change.
No A2a2c2 or later task implementation and no push.

known_limitations: No Core, Detail, Reference, or Annotation Mapper Python implementation exists.
No database verification, Repository connection, Session, Unit of Work, migration, Parser/Indexer, API, or UI exists.
Frozen Domain/ORM repository_root naming is misleading and Manifest v1 lacks a separate logical repository identity.
ImplementationArtifact lacks explicit location_kind, although current Domain prefix semantics are deterministic.
Manifest v1 and current ORM do not persist Mapper or technical identity algorithm versions.
Context/Manifest schema v1 cannot encode exact next task QM2-P0-002A2a2c2 in machine arrays, so legal parent IDs are retained.
unresolved_questions: When will a repository identity ADR approve repository_id/execution_repository_path naming and historical ingestion binding?
Will Manifest v2 add explicit artifact location_kind and Mapper/identity versions?
Where will identity algorithm versions be persisted before durable indexing?
rollback_information: Revert the single containing commit. No Mapper runtime, database, schema, migration, data, API, dependency, lockfile, configuration, accepted ADR, business service, or Factor Lab rollback is required.
security_impact: Contract requires safe structured errors without full objects, commands, reasons, descriptions, credentials, database URLs, or machine-local paths; vectors contain no secret.
data_lineage_impact: No data changed; deterministic versioned technical identities and explicit logical repository binding are now required for future derived Ledger indexing.
